source.title: Layered Unlearning for Adversarial Relearning
source.authors: Timothy Qian; Vinith M. Suriyakumar; Ashia Wilson; Dylan Hadfield-Menell

record.tranche_reason: The study tests fine-tuning recovery after unlearning and refines the claim: layered unlearning reduces recovery in many conditions, while corpus-based fine-tuning can recover more than MCQ-based fine-tuning. It reports results for standard and layered methods.
record.gate_note: The paper tests relearning with MCQ and corpus fine-tuning, not unrelated-data fine-tuning, activation-direction ablation, quantization, or prompt-only attacks. Its proposed inhibitor account is not itself evidence that an activation direction restores knowledge or that knowledge is only blocked from access. Rows below cover the WMDP three-fold comparisons in Table 3, WMDP three-fold unlearned accuracy, selected Years results, and WMDP retain accuracy. Other reported experiments are noted in rows_left_out.
record.test_reason: The study reruns subset-relearning attacks on Zephyr-7B-β after RMU and SimNPO unlearning of WMDP and Years. Unlearning reaches near chance with MMLU retained, yet fine-tuning on one forgotten fold recovers held-out folds (bears on A and B). It also proposes Layered Unlearning as a counter-method and measures its resistance to MCQ and corpus relearning (bears on F). It argues that recovery depends on fold order and attack type.
record.authors_conclusion: Broadly right. The authors conclude that LU improves robustness to fine-tuning relearning across synthetic and LLM benchmarks, and that it blocks recovery of earlier folds, directionally for L-RMU and more symmetrically but weaker for L-SimNPO. Corpus-based fine-tuning is a stronger attack that erodes this robustness, and they conclude forgetting is inherently brittle.
record.recipe_differences: The study uses RMU and SimNPO with a fold-based relearning evaluation, and adds its sequential Layered Unlearning variants. Its recovery evaluation uses MCQ or corpus fine-tuning on forgotten folds and reports best validation accuracy; it is not presented as a direct replication of every method in the claim.
record.method_sensitivity: Results vary with unlearning method (RMU versus SimNPO and their layered variants), dataset, fold order/subset, and relearning data (MCQ versus corpus). The authors report that LU's robustness is sensitive to fold order; corpus fine-tuning is generally stronger for the RMU variants.

fits_no_version.finding: In toy settings (2D logistic regression, bigram transformer), relearning B restores 93% and 73% of task A. Substituting LU's QK/OV attention weights into the standard-unlearned model carries most of LU's robustness (Tables 1, 2, 4).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In non-LLM toy models, relearning generalization after unlearning occurs, and resistance to it localizes in attention components.

record.problems: LLM experiments use Zephyr-7B-β only. The evidence is limited to the tested benchmarks and fold-based relearning; several unlearned accuracies are above the stated 0.25 random-guessing level. LLM relearning tables provide no uncertainty estimates. The reported best validation accuracy is selected across epochs. Retain accuracy is checked on MMLU, not a broad range of capabilities.
record.rows_left_out: The 60-row cap is reached. Omitted synthetic-task results (Tables 1-2 and Appendix Tables 4-5), WMDP two- and four-fold results (Appendix Tables 8 and 10), the remaining WMDP three-fold combinations (Appendix Table 9), most MMLU and Years relearning results (Appendix Tables 11-12), and other unlearned-accuracy/retain-accuracy rows. The selected WMDP three-fold results include all Table 3 comparisons; selected Years rows show cross-dataset variation.

untested.parts: Only RMU and SimNPO, one model (Zephyr-7B-β). No WHP-style or other methods. Prompting, quantization and internal-edit attacks are not tried.
No relearning on unrelated or loosely related data; the authors say they do not address harmless fine-tuning. Only one attack hyperparameter setting (lr 1e-6, batch 4).
Not tested in LLMs. The inhibitor account is a hypothesis, and component substitution is done only in a toy transformer.
No rephrasing, jailbreak, multilingual or in-context attacks.
LU is tested only against fine-tuning relearning at fixed hyperparameters. Not tested against internal edits, quantization, prompting, or stronger fine-tuning budgets.

missing.what: Recovery-rate ratios of each L-method versus its base method, e.g. L-RMU 0.06 and L-RMU-Split 0.00 for relearn C → A MCQ, and values above 1 in forward and corpus cases
MMLU 3-fold: L-RMU backward MCQ recovery 0.30-0.33 vs RMU 0.52-0.53, while corpus recovers 0.54-0.65 for RMU. Declared omitted, but needed for F's cross-dataset comparison

record.verdict_notes: The paper gives no pre-unlearning WMDP or Years accuracy, so how fully relearning restores knowledge cannot be judged; B rows stay partial. Forget accuracy is the best across epochs, and there is a single attack hyperparameter setting. SimNPO was reimplemented because the public checkpoint did not unlearn the folds, and the WMDP RMU is the official checkpoint. This study is not an original source for any version.

versions.untested_parts: The study tests RMU and SimNPO, with and without LU, using MCQ and corpus relearning on one model and benchmarks. It does not test other unlearning methods or the internal-edit, quantization, or prompting attacks named in the version.
Tests relearning on subsets of forgotten folds using MCQ prompts or corpus text. Does not test unrelated or loosely related examples that are not drawn from the forgotten data.

No activation-direction ablation or direct demonstration that the tested LLM methods block access rather than delete knowledge. Synthetic component substitution is not a test of the version as stated.
No prompt rephrasing, jailbreak, language variation, or in-context-information attack.
Tests LU against MCQ- and corpus-based fine-tuning. Does not test its resistance to internal edits, quantization, or prompting attacks.

tranche.reason: Reruns Deeb & Roger's subset relearning on RMU and SimNPO, which recovers held-out folds (bears on A and B). It also shows its own counter-method resists only in one direction and loses to corpus attacks (F partial). T5 is defensible; T1 (for B) and T3 would also fit.

source_check.notes: All values are maximum validation accuracy over epochs (upper bounds). The paper's own chance band is 0.25 +/- 3 SD (threshold 0.35), so the L-RMU backward values 0.26-0.34 sit within it. No pre-unlearning WMDP/Years accuracy is reported. One author (Hadfield-Menell) is shared with an original, so this is not an independent test.

statements.correction: 2505.09500 R05: Zephyr-7B-β, WMDP 3 folds, RMU, relearn on fold A with MCQ, evaluate fold B: 0.24 -> 0.41 (max validation accuracy over epochs). The study shares an author with an original (Lynch et al. 2024), so it is not an independent test.
statements.problem: Gives no figure for this study, which it cites via R05. Its why line says 'No shared-author flag', but this study shares an author (Hadfield-Menell) with an original.

statements.correction: L-RMU, relearn fold C, evaluate fold A, MCQ: WMDP 0.15 -> 0.26 (RMU 0.43); Years 0.29 -> 0.29 (RMU 0.54). The cut is backward only: forward MCQ gives 0.40-0.50 vs RMU 0.41-0.46.

Zephyr-7B-β, WMDP 3 folds, relearn A, evaluate B: RMU MCQ 0.41, corpus 0.45; L-RMU MCQ 0.40, corpus 0.49 (Table 3). Paper: corpus fine-tuning adds 5% on average for RMU; for L-RMU 10% (later->earlier) and 6% (earlier->later).
statements.problem: 0.41 and 0.45 are standard RMU (R05, R06), not Layered RMU as stated. L-RMU A->B is 0.40 (MCQ) and 0.49 (corpus). The corpus > MCQ point holds for both.

statements.correction: L-RMU, relearn a later fold, evaluate an earlier fold (Zephyr-7B-β): WMDP MCQ 0.26 vs RMU 0.43 (R39), 0.31 vs 0.41 (R23), 0.34 vs 0.39 (R47); Years MCQ 0.29 vs 0.54 (R59), corpus 0.32 vs 0.58 (R60). The attack data are forgotten folds, not benign data.
statements.problem: Gives no figure for this study. Its conditions are benign, unrelated or out-of-domain fine-tuning, but this study relearns on forgotten folds and says it does not address harmless fine-tuning. The study supports F only for later-to-earlier relearning.

statements.correction: L-RMU relearn C, eval A, MCQ: 0.26 vs RMU 0.43 (R39); relearn B, eval A: 0.31 vs 0.41 (R23). Earlier-to-later MCQ: L-RMU 0.40, 0.50, 0.50 vs RMU 0.41, 0.45, 0.46 (R07, R15, R31). Corpus earlier-to-later: 0.49, 0.54, 0.54 vs RMU 0.45, 0.49, 0.48 (R08, R16, R32).
statements.problem: Numbers are right, but 0.26 vs 0.43 is R39 (relearn C, eval A), which isn't cited. Cited R23 is 0.31 vs 0.41. Cited corpus rows R08/R16/R32 are unused. This study's own verdicts on these rows are supports/limits_scope, not challenges.

statements.correction: L-RMU: relearn C, eval A, MCQ 0.26 (R39); relearn A, eval B, MCQ 0.40 (R07). L-SimNPO is more symmetric: C->A MCQ 0.42, A->C MCQ 0.41, A->B MCQ 0.41 (Table 3).
statements.problem: Gives no figure for this study. The cited rows R07 and R39 are both L-RMU, so they don't compare base methods. The base-method contrast (L-RMU vs L-SimNPO) is in uncited rows.

reader_labels.label: challenges
reader_labels.condition: WMDP fold relearning conditions on RMU and SimNPO, including MCQ and corpus fine-tuning
reader_labels.reason: Relearning raises accuracy above the corresponding unlearned value in the reported conditions, so simple fine-tuning does recover some targeted performance; see R05-R06, R09-R10, R13-R14, R17-R18, R21-R22, R25-R26, R29-R30, R33-R34, R37-R38, R41-R42, R45-R46 and R49-R50.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: Standard RMU and SimNPO, WMDP three-fold relearning
reader_labels.reason: Fine-tuning on one forgotten fold increases accuracy on other folds compared with unlearned accuracy, though the gains are incomplete; see the linked standard-method rows.

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: Layered methods and corpus-based relearning, including the selected Years condition
reader_labels.reason: LU reduces recovery in some comparisons but does not prevent it consistently; corpus fine-tuning often gives larger increases, while the selected Years L-RMU/MCQ result shows no increase. Recovery is therefore method-, data-, and fold-dependent; see R07-R08, R11-R12, R15-R16, R19-R20, R23-R24, R27-R28, R31-R32, R35-R36, R39-R40, R43-R44, R47-R48, R51-R52 and R57-R60.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: Layered RMU and layered SimNPO on WMDP three-fold relearning
reader_labels.reason: Compared with their non-layered counterparts, layered methods often show smaller recovery, especially for MCQ relearning; see the linked L-RMU and L-SimNPO rows alongside their standard-method counterparts.

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: Corpus-based attacks and selected Years results
reader_labels.reason: LU is not uniformly resistant: corpus fine-tuning still increases accuracy in many conditions, and the Years outcomes vary by attack type; see R08, R12, R16, R20, R24, R28, R32, R36, R40, R44, R48, R52 and R57-R60.
